edition.sessionCovered: Mon, Nov 9 (Brent slides to $97.67 as Trump hints Iran deal · BTC $74,868 · Gold bids $4,100 · CPI Tuesday)
edition.stripNote: Mon 9 Nov. Brent falls 0.6% to $97.67 after Trump says fresh Iran strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress. IRGC claims three more tankers hit in Hormuz on Saturday. Gold bids near $4,100 on safe-haven flows ahead of Tuesday's CPI. BTC slips to $74,868 as crypto tracks risk-off mood. October CPI (Tue) is the week's pivotal release — consensus 3.9% annual.
edition.scoreboardCaption: Mon 9 Nov vs Fri 6 Nov close. Ranked best to worst.
edition.commodleHint: The October consumer _____ index, due Tuesday, is expected to show 3.9% annual inflation and will likely determine the Fed's December decision

overview: Oil led Monday's moves as Brent crude fell 0.6% to $97.67 per barrel after President Trump told CNN that fresh strikes on Iran are 'highly unlikely' as long as negotiations progress. The remark eased the geopolitical premium modestly, though the IRGC's claim of hitting three more oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday — confirmed by UK maritime authorities for at least two vessels — kept risk elevated. WTI slipped to $90.51. The week ahead is dominated by Tuesday's October CPI report, with consensus expecting annual inflation of 3.9%, up from 3.7% in September. A hot print would reinforce the 85% probability of a December rate hike already priced into CME FedWatch. Key earnings from CoreWeave (Tuesday), Cisco and Applied Materials (Thursday) will test the AI infrastructure narrative after last week's tech rout. The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,377 — down 2.7% on the week, its worst since the April 2025 tariff shock. The VIX remains elevated near 25.6. Secretary of State Rubio meets G7 foreign ministers in Paris on Monday for discussions expected to include Iran.

Gold found a bid near $4,100 per ounce, rising roughly 1% from Friday's $4,060 close as investors sought safety ahead of the CPI report and amid continued Hormuz uncertainty. Silver firmed to $52.80. Bitcoin slipped below $75,000 to $74,868, extending losses with a 1% decline as spot ETF outflows reached $1.3 billion over five sessions and risk appetite remained fragile — the Fear and Greed Index sits at 34. Ethereum fell 4.4% to $2,135, underperforming BTC as the ETH/BTC ratio slid to 0.0295. Copper steadied near $6.27 per pound, bouncing modestly from its lowest level since July as the dollar held firm on rate-hike expectations. Platinum firmed to $1,549. The CENTCOM creation of Task Force Iron Gate — extending the naval blockade to Iran's land and Caspian Sea routes — adds a new dimension to the supply disruption. China's November 27 deadline to re-impose export controls on antimony, gallium, germanium and superhard materials looms as a critical watchpoint for strategic mineral supply chains.

watchItems.title: October CPI on Tuesday: the make-or-break data point for December
watchItems.text: The October consumer price index, due Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. ET, is expected to show annual headline inflation of 3.9%, up from 3.7% in September. Core CPI is forecast at 0.3% month-over-month. A hot print would cement the 85% probability of a December 8–9 FOMC hike and could push gold below $4,000 support while strengthening the dollar further. A soft print could lift risk assets and ease rate-hike expectations. Friday's blowout NFP (+165K) already tilted the data mix hawkish, so the bar for a dovish CPI surprise is high. Producer prices (PPI) follow on Friday.

watchItems.title: Trump hints at Iran deal, but IRGC hits three more tankers
watchItems.text: Mixed signals dominate the Iran theatre. Trump told CNN that fresh strikes are 'highly unlikely' if talks progress, calling for 'a very strong agreement.' Yet hours earlier, the IRGC claimed it targeted three oil tankers making 'unauthorized' transits in the Strait of Hormuz, with UK authorities confirming incidents involving at least two vessels. CENTCOM created Task Force Iron Gate to extend the blockade to land and Caspian Sea routes, and the US disabled the M/V Huda for attempting to breach the naval blockade. Secretary Rubio meets G7 foreign ministers in Paris on Monday. The contradiction between diplomatic hints and continued attacks keeps oil's geopolitical premium intact.

watchItems.title: China's Nov 27 export-control deadline: antimony, gallium, germanium at risk
watchItems.text: China's suspension of its prohibition on gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard material exports to the US expires November 27. The original ban was imposed in December 2024 under Document No. 46, and the suspension — announced November 9, 2025, as part of the Busan truce — has not restored meaningful export volumes. With gallium still near $2,100/kg (up 130%+ since early 2025), antimony at ¥93,500/t, and tungsten APT surging past $3,300/mtu, re-imposition would tighten already critical supply chains for semiconductors, ammunition and hardened steel.

watchItems.title: Tech correction deepens: Nvidia reports Nov 17, CoreWeave Tuesday
watchItems.text: The Nasdaq Composite sits in correction territory, down over 12% from its October 6 high, after last week's tech rout. CoreWeave — whose financing underpins much of the AI data-centre buildout — reports Q3 results on Tuesday with an expected loss of $1.45 per share. Applied Materials and Cisco report Thursday. Nvidia's November 17 earnings are the week's main event, with investors watching for any fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's reported relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Spot Bitcoin ETF outflows of $1.3 billion in five sessions underscore the broad risk-off shift. The VIX remains elevated near 25.6.

desk.name: Gold
desk.m: Rebounded from $4,060 Fri · safe-haven bid ahead of CPI · Goldman target $4,150
desk.sum: Gold rose roughly 1% to approximately $4,100 per ounce on Monday, recovering from Friday's NFP-driven drop to $4,060 as investors sought safety ahead of Tuesday's October CPI report. The Strait of Hormuz remains a live risk factor after the IRGC claimed to hit three more tankers on Saturday. Goldman Sachs' reduced year-end target of $4,150 now sits close to spot. Central bank buying — 321 tonnes in Q3, up 42% year-over-year — continues to provide structural support. A hot CPI print could push gold back toward $4,000 support on reinforced hike expectations.

desk.name: Silver
desk.m: Rebounded from $51.90 · gold-silver ratio narrows to ~77.7 · +7.5% on 2 weeks
desk.sum: Silver rallied to approximately $52.80 per ounce, rising 1.7% as it tracked gold's safe-haven bid ahead of CPI. The gold-silver ratio tightened modestly to around 77.7. Silver has gained approximately 7.5% over two weeks, supported by both precious-metals demand and industrial consumption from solar panel manufacturing. The dual demand profile gives silver leverage on both risk-on and risk-off days. Industrial demand from electronics and photovoltaics continues to underpin the long-term outlook.

desk.name: Oil
desk.m: WTI $90.51 · Trump hints deal 'highly unlikely' to need strikes · IRGC hits 3 tankers Sat
desk.sum: Brent fell 0.64% to $97.67 per barrel on Monday, dipping more than $1 at the open after Trump told CNN that fresh Iran strikes are 'highly unlikely' if talks progress. WTI slipped to $90.51. The IRGC's claim of hitting three more oil tankers in the Hormuz Strait on Saturday partially offset the diplomatic signal. CENTCOM's new Task Force Iron Gate extends the blockade to Iran's land and Caspian Sea routes. Eurasia Group maintains only a 10% chance of a negotiated resolution. The market remains trapped between diplomatic hopes and operational reality in the strait.

desk.name: Copper
desk.m: LME ~$13,800/t · bounced from July low · Chile output still at 2-decade low
desk.sum: Copper edged up 0.8% to approximately $6.27 per pound (about $13,800 per tonne), bouncing modestly from its lowest level since July. The recovery came despite a firm dollar, as Chinese demand and tight Chilean supply provided fundamental support. Copper has lost about 6.5% over the past month, pressured by the broader risk-off environment and AI-sector concerns weighing on industrial metals sentiment. Chile's Q3 output remains at its lowest in at least two decades. Shanghai spot premiums remain elevated.

desk.name: Coal
desk.m: Flat on month · up 40% YTD per Kalkine · Hormuz-driven LNG tightness supports coal
desk.sum: Newcastle coal trades near $144 per tonne, easing modestly. Coal has risen approximately 40% year-to-date according to Kalkine, driven by the Hormuz-related LNG supply disruption that has revived coal demand for power generation. Coal-to-gas switching economics continue to favour coal in Asia with JKM LNG prices elevated above $34/MMBtu. The QatarEnergy force majeure — 38 cargoes suspended since April — keeps LNG tight. Any diplomatic breakthrough on Iran would weigh on coal demand by easing energy supply concerns.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.m: Up ~8% over 2 weeks · auto catalyst + hydrogen demand · WPIC deficit narrative
desk.sum: Platinum firmed to approximately $1,549 per ounce, gaining nearly 1% on the day. The metal has rallied roughly 8% over two weeks, benefiting from safe-haven demand, the WPIC supply deficit narrative, and recovering auto-sector sentiment. Platinum's dual role as both a precious and industrial metal continues to work in its favour, capturing gold's safe-haven bid while hydrogen electrolysis growth attracts fresh buying. The strong US jobs data eases some auto-demand concerns.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.m: Stabilised above $1,000 · still pressured by NMC-to-LFP battery shift
desk.sum: Palladium rallied 1.7% to approximately $1,021 per ounce, bouncing as broader precious metals gained. Despite the daily strength, palladium's heavily industrial demand profile (85%+ from auto catalysts) leaves it vulnerable to EV-transition concerns, as battery EVs require no catalytic converter. Nornickel's plant overhaul provides some supply-side support. The metal has held above the psychological $1,000 level through the recent risk-off episode.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.m: IRGC hits 3 more tankers Sat · Task Force Iron Gate extends blockade · 10+ incidents since Nov 1
desk.sum: The Strait of Hormuz risk level remains critical. The IRGC claimed on Saturday that it targeted three oil tankers making 'unauthorized' transits; UK maritime authorities confirmed incidents involving at least two vessels. Since November 1, at least 10 shipping incidents have been recorded in the region, with at least two killing seafarers. CENTCOM created Task Force Iron Gate to extend the naval blockade to Iran's land and Caspian Sea trade routes, and disabled the M/V Huda for attempting to breach the blockade. Trump's CNN interview hinted at a deal, calling fresh strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress, but Secretary Rubio's G7 meeting in Paris on Monday suggests the diplomatic track is still nascent. Eurasia Group holds peace odds at 10%.
desk.src: Al Jazeera · Reuters · UKMTO · CBS News

desk.name: Corn
desk.m: Down ~8% m/m · US harvest nearing completion · managed money net short
desk.sum: December corn firmed slightly to approximately 441¢ per bushel, edging up 0.3% on light short-covering. The US corn harvest is nearing completion with yields largely meeting expectations. Managed money remains net short. Corn has lost about 8% over the past month as harvest-season selling pressure weighs. Brazil's safrinha planting progress is on track. Tuesday's CPI report is the next macro catalyst for agricultural markets via its impact on dollar strength.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.m: Down ~16% m/m · dropped to September low · global supply ample
desk.sum: December wheat dropped to approximately 580¢ per bushel, falling to its lowest level since September. Wheat has shed about 16% over the past month as ample global supply, resumed Russian grain shipments and a firm dollar weigh on prices. Record managed-money short positions limit upside. The USDA's next WASDE report will provide updated supply-demand projections. Global wheat production is tracking near record levels for 2026/27.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.m: Down ~8% m/m · harvest pressure easing · Brazilian planting progresses
desk.sum: Soybeans bounced to approximately 1,189¢ per bushel, rising 0.7% on modest bargain-hunting after recent declines. The market has lost about 8% over the past month under harvest-season selling and South American planting progress. Chinese buying interest remains muted. Goldman Sachs notes the global soybean balance remains comfortable. The strong dollar and rate-hike expectations continue to cap export competitiveness.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.m: ETH $2,135 · spot ETF outflows $1.3B in 5 sessions · Fear & Greed at 34
desk.sum: Bitcoin fell 1% to $74,868 on Monday in early Asian trading, extending its slide below $75,000 as risk appetite remained fragile. The crypto market tracked broader tech weakness, with no clear crypto-specific catalyst for the decline. Spot Bitcoin ETF outflows reached approximately $1.3 billion over five sessions through November 6. BTC remains roughly 40% below its all-time high of $126,080. Ethereum fell 4.4% to $2,135, with the ETH/BTC ratio sliding to 0.0295 — its lowest in six weeks. The Fear and Greed Index sits at 34 (Fear). CPI on Tuesday is the key macro catalyst.

desk.name: LNG
desk.m: JKM low-$34s · TTF $34 · HH $2.97 · QatarEnergy force majeure extends
desk.sum: Asian LNG spot (JKM) holds in the low-$34 range per MMBtu for December delivery. QatarEnergy's force majeure extends to at least end-December 2026, with 38 cargoes (about 5 bcm) suspended since April, keeping supply structurally tight. European TTF holds near $34/MBtu, with EU storage at 74.7% — about 17% below the five-year average ahead of winter. Henry Hub firmed to $2.97. The approaching Northern Hemisphere winter and Hormuz uncertainty support prices. Trump's diplomatic hints add modest downside risk if a deal materialises.

desk.name: Sulfur
desk.m: FOB Kuwait $765 · tanker attacks maintain supply squeeze · Nov 27 export-control deadline looms
desk.sum: Sulfur remains elevated with CFR Southeast Asia around $1,200 per tonne. Despite Trump's diplomatic hints, the IRGC's continued tanker attacks maintain the acute supply squeeze on Middle Eastern sulfur shipments, affecting fertiliser and mining supply chains. FOB Kuwait holds near $765 (KPC). SMM analysis notes that the ceiling question remains open after sulfur broke through $1,200. Chinese domestic sulfur holds near 7,200 yuan per tonne. The market remains highly sensitive to any diplomatic breakthrough on Iran.

desk.name: Potash
desk.m: BPC India $383 CFR · China benchmark ~$348 · Argus: demand to remain firm in 2026
desk.sum: Muriate of potash (MOP) CFR Brazil holds near $367 per tonne, largely unchanged. BPC's India contract remains approximately $35 above China's 2026 benchmark at $383 per tonne CFR. Argus Media forecasts potash demand to remain firm through 2026. Belarus and Russia still account for about 40% of global supply despite Western sanctions. The S&P Global specification update for granular MOP CFR Brazil assessments reflects growing market maturity.

desk.name: Antimony
desk.m: Nov 27 deadline for China export-control suspension · Document No. 46 constraining supply
desk.sum: Chinese antimony (#1 ingot) holds near 93,500 yuan per tonne. The critical near-term catalyst is China's November 27 deadline: the suspension of its export prohibition on antimony, gallium, germanium and superhard materials to the US expires that day. The original ban was imposed in December 2024 under Document No. 46, and the Busan truce's suspension has not restored meaningful export volumes. Re-imposition would tighten supply for ammunition, flame retardants and semiconductor manufacturing.

desk.name: Gallium & Germanium
desk.m: Up >130% since early 2025 · Nov 27 suspension deadline · China 98% of supply
desk.sum: Gallium holds near $2,100 per kilogram outside China, up over 130% since early 2025. The November 27 deadline for China's export-control suspension is the key near-term risk. The original prohibition under Document No. 46 has a presumption of denial for US end users, and the Busan truce suspension has not meaningfully restored exports. China produces about 98% of global gallium. The chip-sector turmoil adds demand uncertainty. Western governments are investing billions to build alternative supply chains, but timelines stretch well beyond 2027.

desk.name: Vanadium
desk.m: Down from $5.44 in 2024 · steel demand soft · VRFB adoption uncertain
desk.sum: Vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) holds near $5.02 per pound, soft as steel demand weakens amid the global risk-off environment. The long-term bull case rests on vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFBs) for grid-scale energy storage, but large-scale adoption timing remains uncertain. China, Russia and South Africa control over 90% of supply. The broader macro picture — firm dollar, hawkish Fed expectations — offers little near-term support for industrial metals.

desk.name: Cocoa
desk.m: Stabilised above $5,100 · ICE inventories at 2.5-yr high · Ivory Coast mid-crop concerns
desk.sum: ICE cocoa held near $5,155 per tonne, stabilising after dipping below $5,100 last week. Rising ICE warehouse inventories — now at a 2.5-year high of 3,740,476 bags — continue to pressure prices. A possible 42–50% drop in Ivory Coast's mid-crop adds a bearish undertone for the season ahead. StoneX projects 2026/27 global output could fall 9.6%, potentially turning the current surplus into a deficit. Demand destruction from elevated prices is evident in Q3 grindings data. Cocoa has lost about 7.7% over the past month.

desk.name: Cobalt
desk.m: DRC quotas 96,600 t/yr · flat · NMC-to-LFP shift continues
desk.sum: Cobalt holds at approximately $33,525 per tonne, flat. The DRC (70% of global mine supply) maintains export quotas of 96,600 tonnes per year through 2027 to support prices. However, the EV battery chemistry shift from NMC to LFP continues to structurally reduce cobalt demand. SunSirs reports a reshaping of global cobalt supply entering a new pricing phase. European cobalt has weakened on demand concerns.

desk.name: Lithium
desk.m: Futures ~¥94k · spot ~¥99k · range ¥90k–110k · supply growth outpaces demand
desk.sum: Chinese lithium carbonate futures hold near ¥94,000 per tonne, with spot around ¥99,350. The market remains in the ¥90,000–110,000 trading range established after halving from the mid-May peak above ¥200,000. SMM reports supply growth is outpacing declining demand, with weekly production rising as spodumene-based output expands. Downstream buyers are cautious, purchasing mainly for rigid needs. Goldman Sachs projects a 444,000-tonne global surplus by 2028.

desk.name: Rubber
desk.m: $2.55/kg · SE Asia supply tight · fungal blight ongoing · range-bound outlook
desk.sum: Natural rubber (RSS3) trades near $2,550 per tonne ($2.55/kg), in a range-bound pattern. Southeast Asian supply remains tight with Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia — producing 70% of global latex — still affected by Pestalotiopsis fungal leaf blight. SunSirs forecasts the Chinese spot market to remain range-bound. Auto-sector demand remains solid despite the tech-sector turmoil, supported by replacement-tyre cycles.

desk.name: Uranium
desk.m: Stabilised in mid-$80s · long-term contracts near $94/lb · AI-driven demand · Kazakhstan shortfalls
desk.sum: Uranium spot holds near $86 per pound U₃O₈, stabilised in the mid-$80s range after briefly touching $100 earlier in 2026. Long-term contract prices have risen to near $94/lb — close to $100 — as utilities lock in supply amid energy security concerns. Over 440 reactors operate worldwide with 60+ under construction. AI data-centre power demand is emerging as a structural demand driver. Kazakhstan (43% of mine output) faces production shortfalls due to acid supply constraints. The Sprott Physical Uranium Trust continues to absorb spot supply.

desk.name: Rare Earths
desk.m: China prices fell Nov 3 · Dy and Tb unchanged · Western premiums elevated
desk.sum: Neodymium-praseodymium (NdPr) oxide trades near $75 per kilogram. China's rare earth prices declined on November 3, while dysprosium and terbium quotations held steady. Western buyer premiums remain elevated: dysprosium at $2,500–$5,500/kg and terbium at $10,000–$13,000/kg — well above Chinese domestic rates. China controls about 60% of global mine output and over 90% of processing. The November 27 export-control deadline adds uncertainty to the strategic minerals complex.

desk.name: Manganese
desk.m: South Africa 37% · Gabon 18% · CIF China flat · minor fluctuations
desk.sum: Manganese ore (44% Mn content) trades near $4.40 per dry metric tonne unit CIF China, with minor fluctuations according to SteelOrbis. South Africa supplies about 37% of global ore and Gabon 18%. Steel production consumes 90% of manganese demand. High-purity manganese sulfate for EV batteries is an emerging demand driver. SMM reports miners are maintaining a firm pricing stance and the market is holding up well.

desk.name: Nickel
desk.m: Bounced from recent lows · up ~4% m/m · Indonesia 67% mine · surplus persists
desk.sum: LME nickel edged up 0.4% to approximately $16,385 per tonne, bouncing modestly from recent lows. Nickel has gained about 4% over the past month, partially recovering from September–October weakness. Indonesia's dominance at 67% of global mine output and continued NPI/HPAL expansions keep the market in surplus. However, short-term supply tightness from Chinese smelter maintenance provides some support. The strong dollar and rate-hike expectations remain headwinds for industrial metals.

desk.name: Tin
desk.m: Down ~16% m/m · Myanmar ban · Indonesia curbs · pulled back from highs
desk.sum: LME tin held flat near $45,480 per tonne, consolidating after recent volatility. Tin has lost about 16% over the past month, pulling back sharply from late-September highs. Structural supply constraints persist: Myanmar's Wa State mining ban removed roughly 10% of global supply, and Indonesia continues to tighten export licensing. LME tin stocks remain near historic lows. The broader risk-off mood and stronger dollar have overshadowed the tight fundamental picture.

desk.name: Zinc
desk.m: Pulled back from 4-year highs · TCs deeply negative · smelter cuts continue
desk.sum: LME zinc held near $3,718 per tonne, consolidating after pulling back from recent four-year highs. Treatment charges remain deeply negative, meaning miners effectively pay smelters to process concentrate. Several Chinese and European smelters have cut output. LME inventories have plummeted approximately 64% year-to-date. Zinc has lost about 1.2% over the past month. The fundamental picture remains tight despite the broader risk-off environment weighing on base metals.

desk.name: Tungsten
desk.m: China domestic APT ¥550k/t Nov · concentrates up ¥10k · +200%+ since early 2026
desk.sum: Overseas APT holds above $3,300 per mtu. The Ganzhou Tungsten Association set November domestic APT at 550,000 yuan per tonne (flat month-on-month), with concentrates raised by 10,000 yuan to 375,000 yuan per standard tonne. China's export controls on tungsten processing technology have created a severe non-Chinese supply crisis — Fastmarkets reported tungsten exports fell close to 40% year-over-year. Western prices have nearly quadrupled China's domestic levels. The Busan truce deadline of November 9–10 and January 10 end date keep uncertainty elevated.

desk.name: Helium
desk.m: Up 358% YTD by late April · Ras Laffan repair 3–5 years · Russia export controls to 2027
desk.sum: Grade-A helium trades near $390 per thousand cubic feet, at critical levels. Prices surged 358% year-to-date by late April as the Iran war damaged Qatar's Ras Laffan facilities — repair estimates stretch to 3–5 years — and Russia imposed export controls lasting through 2027. Combined, roughly 40% of global supply was cut or frozen within six weeks. Commercial inventories are at their lowest since 2008. Qatar and the US together supply about 81% of global helium. Semiconductor fabs, MRI machines and space launch consume most demand.

desk.name: Phosphate
desk.m: OCP 30% global · DAP $560/t · sulfur cost surge pressuring phosphate economics
desk.sum: Phosphate rock trades near $120 per tonne FOB Morocco, with Morocco's OCP Group controlling about 30% of global trade and holding 70% of known reserves. DAP (diammonium phosphate) prices sit near $560 per tonne CFR India. The sulfur price surge — up over 31% in two months per SunSirs — is pressuring phosphate production economics, as sulfur is a key input for phosphoric acid. Global phosphate production reached approximately 45 million tonnes. China periodically restricts fertiliser exports to protect domestic supply.
